source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Scrape dried drainage from intact skin beside the wound and submit it in a dry container because surface material is the preferred culture source.","B":"Swab the removed dressing because organisms on an old dressing represent the wound more accurately than material collected from the wound itself.","C":"Swab intact periwound skin because normal skin flora identify the organism responsible for infection within the draining wound.","D":"Collect purulent material or a specimen directly from the wound with the laboratory-approved sterile system and place it in the designated transport medium."}}
source_row.rationale: ARUP's wound-culture collection instructions call for purulent material/aspirate or a swab specimen collected from the wound and placed in the designated transport system. Option D samples the actual wound rather than old dressing material or intact surrounding skin. Options A, B, and C preferentially sample surface contamination or normal flora and do not follow the laboratory collection method. NCSBN places obtaining nonblood specimens for diagnostic testing under Reduction of Risk Potential.
source_row.source_detail: ARUP Test 0060132, Wound Culture and Gram Stain — Specimen Required: collect aspirate/purulent material or a swab specimen from the wound; swab specimens are placed in the laboratory-designated ESwab transport medium. Anaerobic culture requires appropriate deeper specimen/transport when indicated. Current ARUP Laboratories test directory entry 0060132; collection requirements live-rechecked 2026-08-15. Blueprint corrected to Reduction of Risk Potential because the item tests collection of a nonblood diagnostic specimen, an explicit 2026 NCSBN laboratory-values activity. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Reduction of Risk Potential: diagnostic probability tools, laboratory/tumor-marker interpretation, ECG/lab monitoring and potential complications. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
